extraction.name: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
extraction.description: This paper presents a systematic study on object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), evaluating several representative models and proposing a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The study uses existing datasets (MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, GQA) and does not involve new data collection.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MSCOCO (Lin et al., 2014), A-OKVQA (Schwenk et al., 2022), GQA (Hudson and Manning, 2019).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For POPE, negative objects are sampled using Random, Popular, and Adversarial strategies to construct evaluation questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images are processed using visual encoders from LVLMs; for SEEM-based POPE, automatic segmentation with SEEM tool is used to annotate objects.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (ground-truth objects) are from human-labeled datasets (MSCOCO) or automated with SEEM for unannotated datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SEEM (Zou et al., 2023) for automatic segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Consistency analysis between POPE responses and model-generated captions shows strong correlation, validating reliability.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Hallucination in LVLMs can degrade performance and harm user experiences in real-world applications like autonomous driving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LVLMs are prone to hallucinate frequently appearing or co-occurring objects in visual instruction datasets, influenced by unbalanced object distributions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Evaluation limited to object hallucination, not overall model capacity; results may be affected by data distribution; POPE may misclassify if models don't explicitly answer 'Yes'/'No'; SEEM annotations may diverge from human labels; only a small number of LVLMs evaluated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for evaluating object hallucination in LVLMs; not recommended for overall performance assessment.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For POPE, 6 questions per image (3 ground-truth, 3 negative objects).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (Zou et al., 2023), ChatGPT for VQA evaluation assistance.
